info.name: Statement Delivery Platform
info.description: Exercises the Delivery.Api (8081) and Download.Gateway (8082) end to end - happy paths, denial paths, and the compliance flows. Derived from the running APIs' OpenAPI documents at /openapi/v1.json. Import the local environment, run top to bottom (folder 02 before 03), and read postman/README.md for the single-use caveat and the findings. Tokens are minted in-band from /v1/dev/tokens; no credential is stored in this file.

item.name: 00 Setup
item.description: Health, ping, in-band token minting, and resolving a real customer + statement. The collection-level pre-request already mints the four JWTs; these requests prove the stack is reachable and capture the statement id + partition key that everything downstream needs.

request.description: Liveness: process is up. No dependencies consulted.
Readiness: dependency booleans. 200 with a live DB/object store; 503 when a dependency is down. Asserted as either so the request is honest on a partial stack.
Build identity for operators.

Lists customer A's statements and captures the first result's id and period.start into statementId / statementPeriod. Needs seeded data; skips capture cleanly if the list is empty so the folder still passes on an unseeded stack (later data folders will then report the missing id).

exec: // A DISCOVERY request, not a property test: its job is to capture ids. On a seeded
// stack it is 200 and captures; on an unseeded DB it is 404; on a host with no
// database at all it is 5xx. All are tolerated with a warning so the setup folder is
// honest about the stack it was pointed at - the data folders then report the gap.
console.warn('customer A has no statements - seed data before the data folders.');
' - the data folders (01-08) need the full stack (DB + object store) to pass.');

item.name: 01 Catalogue
item.description: The customer statement list and single-statement lookup. Proves the mandatory date-range contract (partition pruning), cursor round-trip, and that NO crypto material ever appears in a catalogue response.

request.description: Runs only meaningfully when the first page set nextCursor. An opaque cursor that round-trips is the pagination contract.
The date range is REQUIRED - it is what lets the query prune partitions.
Single lookup. The period is the partition key - omitting it is a 400 (next request).

exec: pm.test('has id and status', () => { pm.expect(b).to.have.property('id'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status'); });

item.description: Issue a single-use link, redeem it, and prove the PDF plus every security header. MUST run before folder 03, which replays this token. The redeemed URL is cleared immediately after use (see README, 'single-use').

request.description: Redeems the capability URL. The token IS the credential, so no Authorization header.

item.name: 03 Download — denials
item.description: Every way a redemption legitimately fails, and the property that matters most: the denials are byte-identical. A reviewer running this folder SEES the uniform denial rather than reading about it. Runs after 02 so the replay case has a spent token to reuse.

request.description: Redeems the SAME url folder 02 already spent (02 kept a copy in spentUrl for exactly this). A single-use token consumed once must be a 404 on the second redemption.

exec: if (!pm.environment.get('spentUrl')) console.warn('no spentUrl - run folder 02 first');

request.description: Issues a link (pre-request), DELETEs it, then redeems. Expect 404.

exec: if (e1 || issue.code !== 201) { console.warn('issue failed for revoke case'); return; }

request.description: A value that is not even the right shape. Per the source (TokenSecret.TryParse -> DenyAsync) this is a uniform 404, never a 400 that would confirm the encoding.
43 base64url chars that decode cleanly but match no row.
Customer B asking for a link to A's statement. Ownership is a predicate: 404, indistinguishable from a statement that does not exist.
The most valuable assertion in the collection. Compares the bodies captured above. Any difference between denial causes is an information oracle.

exec: const bodies = keys.map(k => pm.environment.get(k)).filter(b => b !== undefined && b !== '');
pm.test('captured at least two denial bodies', () => pm.expect(bodies.length).to.be.above(1));
pm.test('all denials are byte-identical', () => bodies.forEach(b => pm.expect(b).to.eql(bodies[0])));

item.name: 04 Audit
item.description: Chain verification and scope. NOTE: the per-statement access-log endpoint the brief asks for does not exist in this API (see README, 'Findings'); verification of access events is via the audit chain, not a REST access-log resource.

request.description: An ordinary customer token must not read the audit trail.

item.name: 05 Compliance — legal hold
item.description: Place holds at both scopes (statement and customer), list active holds, release. Holds are what block erasure in folder 06.

exec: // Kept ACTIVE into folder 06, which proves the LEGAL_HOLD erasure block against it, then releases it.
// Contract shape (OpenAPI): { holds: [...], cursor } - not { items }.

request.description: DELETE carries a body (ReleaseHoldRequest.releaseReason) - see README, 'Findings', the brief showed this route without one.

item.name: 06 Compliance — erasure
item.description: Crypto-erasure lifecycle. Assertions are on the PAYLOAD - a bare 409 passes a status check and still fails the requirement, so the citations (reason, caseReference, basis, retainUntil) are asserted explicitly. DPO scope required.

request.description: With a customer hold from folder 05 in force, erasure is refused and CITES the hold.
Releases the customer-scoped hold placed in 05 so the next request sees retention alone, and so a second run starts clean.

No hold is active any more, so the only thing standing between the DPO and erasure is the statute. A bare 409 would pass a status assertion and fail the requirement, so the basis and the date are asserted.
Erasure sits ABOVE the operator scope: audit.verify alone must not schedule it.

204 when a scheduled erasure is cancelled; 404 when none is scheduled. The brief expects 204 and the code returns exactly that (Results.NoContent), though the OpenAPI document mislabels it 200 - see README, 'Findings'.

item.name: 07 Archive & restore
item.description: The archived-statement download path: 409 with a working restoreEndpoint, then restore, poll, download. Needs a statement in ARCHIVED state - see README, 'Known limitations'.

item.name: Download link on archived statement is 409

request.description: When the statement is ARCHIVED the link issue is a 409 carrying restoreEndpoint. On an AVAILABLE statement this is a 201 instead - both are asserted so the folder is honest whatever state the seed left.

exec: // Not archived (409): nothing to poll - see README, Known limitations.

request.description: Bounded poll: re-queues itself up to a few times until AVAILABLE, then moves on.

exec: if (st !== 'AVAILABLE' && n < 5) { setTimeout(()=>{}, 1000); pm.execution.setNextRequest('Poll restore status'); }

item.name: 08 Operations
item.description: Statement runs and reconciliation. Demonstrates run idempotency (same period -> same runId) and a clean reconciliation.

request.description: Same period must return the SAME runId, not a second run.
Requeues every quarantined item in the run (all=true), or a specific set via itemIds. 200/204 on a real run; 404 when runId is unset on an unseeded stack.

/latest is the most recent COMPLETED run, and the retention worker picks a requested run up on its own cadence (~60 s), so this request re-queues itself until the run triggered above is the one it is reading. Reading it once would report the PREVIOUS run.

exec: // Not our run yet: wait for the worker, then read again (bounded: 20 x 5 s).
pm.test('latest is the run triggered above', () => pm.expect(b.runId).to.eql(want));

item.name: 09 Security probes
item.description: IDOR and scope. The property throughout: a resource you do not own is 404, never 403 - a 403 would confirm the resource exists. Plus the gateway's deliberate unauthenticated posture.

request.description: Customer B's token against customer A's collection.

exec: pm.test('404 or 403 - and we assert the safe one', () => pm.expect([403,404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: IDOR: B reads A's statement by id

request.description: A protected Delivery.Api route with no Authorization header.

item.name: No auth on the gateway is 404

request.description: The gateway is deliberately unauthenticated - the token IS the credential - so an unknown token is a 404, not a 401.

exec: // Collection pre-request: fail fast if the API is down, then mint the four dev JWTs in-band.
// The dev-token endpoint (/v1/dev/tokens) signs with the stack's own key, so a fresh clone needs
// no side quest - but the endpoint is Development-only, and the tokens carry sub = customerId.
if (pm.environment.get(envKey)) { return done(); }   // already set - never re-mint
console.error(`mint ${envKey} returned ${res.code}. Is the API in Development? ${res.text()}`);
// Chain them so the requests complete before the actual request runs.
// DPO scope stacks ON staff: the endpoint only adds erasure.execute when BOTH flags are set.
// Applied to EVERY response: nothing internal may leak, and every error must carry a traceId.
pm.test('no internal detail in response', function () {
// traceId is a promise of Delivery.Api's problem+json errors. Two deliberate exceptions:
//  - the gateway's 404 is BYTE-IDENTICAL across every denial (ADR-0015/16); a per-request
//    traceId would make each one distinguishable, so it carries none (folder 03 proves this).
//  - the erasure 409 is a decision payload ({reason, basis, retainUntil, ...}, application/json),
//    not a problem document; folder 06 asserts its fields directly.
